HVA is real-space and its hopping gates do not conserve momentum, so it cannot run in the fixed-$\mathbf K$ sector: `trotter_realspace.jl` lifts basis, Hamiltonian and target into the full occupation basis by the Slater-determinant Fourier change of basis, verified against ED energies to $\sim10^{-13}$ at startup. (b) **A symmetry obstruction that constrains how the comparison may be run:** tie=full and tie=spin tie a bond's $\uparrow/\downarrow$ gates to one coefficient, so the circuit commutes with spin exchange $P$; our Slater reference fills a degenerate level on different orbitals per spin, giving $\langle\mathrm{ref}|P|\mathrm{ref}\rangle=0$ while the ED target has $P=-1$, capping reachable fidelity at exactly $0.5$ at any depth (measured 0.4999 at 2, 4, 12, 14 layers; 0.9996 at tie=none, 4 layers). A related failure on $3\times3\,(3,3)$ — infidelity stuck at 0.836 — traced to that system having no Slater non-interacting state at all, and prompted a `--ref=slater|eigenstate` flag; from an eigenstate reference it moves 1.31e-2 (P=1) → 1.57e-3 (P=7), still flattening, with P=1 buying bitwise zero improvement. questions.title: Hardware-depth estimate
questions.why: one momentum-space rotation under (a) Jordan–Wigner, (b) native fermionic gates, (c) FFFT to real space; then the pruned layer for $4\times3$. Inputs verified (`notes/momentum-basis-precedents-2026-09-11.md`, item 9): Yordanov 2020, $2n_{df}+5$ CNOTs per JW double on index span $n_{df}$; FFFT $O(N^{1.5})$/$O(\sqrt N)$ on a 2D array (Jiang 2018), $O(N\log N)$/$O(N)$ planar (Babbush 2018); run on 27 modes (Granet 2026). Claude's back-of-envelope, in ¶7 and ¶18 until replaced: $n_{df}\le24$ → ≲53 CNOTs per rotation × ~680 ≈ $3\times10^4$; for scale, Willow 2025 used 4,372 two-qubit gates, Cade 2020's HVA on 3×4 ≈ $10^3$ at $U=2$. Tamra's channel reply (2026-09-12): a platform-agnostic gate count is the precise measure; JW cost depends on the encoding of the 2D lattice. *Task `86akhca09`.* **2026-09-21:** an analytic handle for our side, from Jonathon's reading — Barkoutsos 2018 (PRA 98, 022322) gives $2N+3$ layers for a two-body unitary spanning $N$ sites between its extreme indices, with overlapping Pauli strings blocking concurrency. The structural consequence should be said plainly when this is written: **our ansatz is inherently deeper than HVA**, which keeps its gates local by construction. That is the honest cost side of the trade this item exists to price.

questions.title: The small-dimension energy floor of the exact exponential
questions.why: rerun at dim ≲ $10^2$ with tight Krylov tolerance and more iterations; pre-registered readings: (i) artifact → "comparable, cheaper"; (ii) real → "the fidelity landscape is easier than the energy landscape." (b) A loader bug was found: the *Trotter* path also had `suffix="noreg"` hardcoded, matched no files, returned all-NaN, and fell back to the original `barren_study` runs — which had stopped at the driver default `--maxiters=100`, a 303-iteration cap at $|g|\sim10^{-3}$, against an exponential curve run to $|g|\sim3\times10^{-5}$. Every earlier panel (a) was therefore comparing a converged exponential against a truncated Trotter. All ten systems were re-run at `--maxiters=1000` under `--run_label=barren_study_mi1000` (the original files are left alone because panel (c) reads them), and `testing/verify_trotter_opt_run_label.jl` asserts the curve now resolves to the re-runs. Result at $U=8$: for $\dim\mathcal H\ge392$ the exponential beats optimized Trotter by 3–9× on both infidelity and energy error — the expected ordering — while at $\dim\mathcal H=50$ and $68$ optimized Trotter reaches $\sim10^{-13}$ infidelity and machine-precision energy against the exponential's $2\times10^{-8}$–$2\times10^{-6}$. The extra iterations improved the Trotter side there, so **the small-dimension gap is wider than before, not closed**. Caveat to state when writing it: several `mi1000` runs still hit the 1000-iteration cap (only one converged on gradient tolerance), so "under-converged" is reduced, not eliminated, as a contributor.

questions.title: HVA benchmark: Cade's public code, or rebuilt in our codebase?
questions.why: Tamra · no task yet · raised 2026-09-14. Jonathon estimates about a day using their code; Tamra up to a week building it, and wants to read the paper first to confirm the gate ordering and which loss Cade used — likely energy. Jonathon holds that the gradient code works regardless of ansatz and the work is the gate ordering; Tamra holds that careful index matching to her existing enumeration is needed to avoid subtle errors. **Gates item 14, which gates the venue.** What "their code" can mean (agent sweep 2026-09-14, repos cloned and read): Cade et al. released no code — the data.bris deposit (`10.5523/bris.39z0ftvswqp0o244kkdultrwlo`) is optimizer logs only, energy and fidelity vs iteration for HV/EHV/NP on every grid incl. `3x4/depth-k`. The ansatz is public in the follow-up's repo, `PhaseCraft/fhvqe-paper` (Stanisic 2022; Apache-2.0; Cirq 0.11 + OpenFermion 1.1, pinned 2021): `fhvqe/circuit.py` has Cade's Eq. (2) split (`onsite_layer`, `horiz_layer`, `vert_layer`, fermionic-swap network), Jordan–Wigner, generic $n_h\times n_v$ builders, and the $U=0$ Slater state by Givens rotations — **but no fidelity and no ED reference**; it optimizes energy through `cirq.Simulator`. Cade's loss was energy (exact energy measurements, L-BFGS). Nothing else public implements HVA for Hubbard with a fidelity: Qiskit's `hamiltonian_variational_ansatz` is generic, ReCirq `fermi_hubbard` is fixed-Trotter dynamics, TenCirChem's Hubbard notebook is UCCSD, Wiersema's `zyglrox` has no fermions. So the "day" path is fhvqe's circuit builder at $4\times3$, 9 electrons (their Table II filling), state-vector, overlapped against the XDiag eigenstate; the data.bris logs are the $U=2$ sanity check. **2026-09-21 — overtaken by events; needs closing rather than deciding.** Neither path was formally chosen, but the rebuild-in-our-codebase option was taken: the ansatz has been implemented, tested (329 tests) and run since 2026-09-17 (item 14). The estimate that settled it in practice was Jonathon's, not the week Tamra feared. What remains of this item is a decision to *record* — including whether Cade's `fhvqe` builder is still wanted as an independent cross-check at $U=2$, which is the one thing our own implementation cannot give us.
